items.title: Immigration Dept gears up for F1 Bahrain GP visitor surge at Sepang
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department (JIM) will ensure that immigration procedures involving visas and related passes at the country’s entry points run smoothly during the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) this October. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department would work closely with the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) to ensure clearance procedures at the country's entry points are carried out efficiently while complying with all security requirements. “We must provide the best possible service to ensure the smooth organisation of the Formula 1 event.

items.title: Immigration busts ‘flying passport’ syndicate, three arrested in Johor
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM) has dismantled a “flying passport” syndicate with the arrest of three suspects at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) in Gelang Patah, Johor, yesterday, said Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban. He said the operation, which began at 10am, involved a team of officers and personnel from the Putrajaya Immigration headquarters Intelligence and Special Operations Division and Johor JIM. He said the team also seized mobile phones, keys to a premise, jewellery, Immigration security stamps and RM20,000 in cash.

items.title: Indonesian maid jailed four years for neglect that led to toddler’s drowning in Sentul pool
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — An Indonesian domestic helper was sentenced to four years’ jail by the Sessions Court here today after she pleaded guilty to neglecting a boy, resulting in his death by drowning in an adult swimming pool last month. According to the charge, Wahyuni, as a person responsible for the care of a two-year-three-month-old boy, neglected the child, resulting in his death. According to the facts of the case, the victim’s mother had instructed the accused, who was employed as her domestic helper, to take the victim and his five-year-old brother to the swimming pool at their residential complex on the day of the incident.

items.title: Remains of three policemen killed in Beaufort electrocution incident sent home after post-mortem
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The remains of three police officers who died believed to be from electrocution outside the Weston Police Station, Beaufort, yesterday afternoon were brought out from the Forensic Department of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital (HQE) at 2:55 pm today to be sent back to their respective hometowns. The remains of Corporal Chiu Teck Siong will be taken to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Air Operations Force (PGU) Airfield here before being flown to Sarawak. Meanwhile, Beaufort District Police Chief Supt Champin Piuh expressed his appreciation to Sabah Police Commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun, members of the Sabah Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK), and HQE for their extensive assistance in facilitating the management of the remains.

items.title: Bersatu sec‑gen Azmin Ali says party remains legitimate Perikatan component despite PAS claim
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) secretary-general Datuk Seri Mohamed Azmin Ali today hit back at PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang’s assertion that the party’s membership in Perikatan Nasional (PN) had automatically lapsed, describing the claim as unconstitutional. He stressed that Bersatu’s position could only be decided by the PN presidential council under Clause 7A of the coalition’s constitution. Therefore, Bersatu remains a legitimate component party of Perikatan Nasional,” Azmin said.

items.title: Border agency seizes falsely declared frozen chicken, pork worth RM3.42m at Sepanggar Port
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 7 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) has seized 12 containers carrying frozen animal products worth an estimated RM3.42 million at Sepanggar Port. The seizure was the result of an enforcement operation targeting false import declarations. AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain said the seizure involved 348,000kg of frozen chicken and pork believed to have been brought into the country through declarations that did not match the cargo.

items.title: Anwar says GLICs deployed RM20.3b in domestic investments under GEAR-uP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — The Government-Linked Enterprises Activation and Reform Programme (GEAR-uP), which is entering its third year, saw government-linked investment companies (GLICs) allocating and deploying RM 20.3 billion domestically. “This (GEAR-uP) is not capital seeking passive returns. Much has been achieved, but much remains to be done,” Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said in the GEAR-uP Progress Report released today.

items.title: Anwar says constituency funds belong to people, not exclusive right of elected MPs
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Aug 7 — Government funding allocated to a parliamentary constituency is intended for its constituents and is not the exclusive right of its elected Member of Parliament (MP), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said the funds were meant to finance facilities and improvements that raised the living standards of the people in the constituency. Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Melaka Police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar.

items.title: Government prioritises new theatres to support surgeries during Sultanah Aminah Hospital upgrades
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 7 — The Economy Ministry will prioritise building three to four new operating theatres at the Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) while the mechanical and electrical (M&E) upgrades take place. Its minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the new operating theatres will complement the hospital’s existing 12 operating theatres that will also undergo part of the M&E upgrades. Akmal Nasrullah said the government will prioritise the building of the operating theatres to support ongoing surgeries and make way for the hospital’s upgrades.

items.title: AGC: Nicky Liow made RM10m payment to compound 26 money laundering charges
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — Businessman Liow Soon Hee, better known as Nicky Liow, paid RM10 million to settle money laundering charges after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) accepted his representation and withdrew 26 counts against him. Liow had faced 26 charges under Section 4 of the Anti Money Laundering, Anti Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613) at the Shah Alam Sessions Court on April 12, 2022. In line with Section 92 of Act 613, the AGC subsequently withdrew all charges against Liow.

items.title: Premises raided as IRB investigates individuals named in Tabung Haji RCI report, discrepancies found
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) has opened investigations into individuals identified in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). In a statement, IRB said a tax risk analysis had found discrepancies between the individuals’ declared income and their asset holdings. “IRB officers had raided several related premises to gather information, examine documents and verify facts relevant to the investigations.

items.title: Four charged in Shah Alam court over false Perkeso Daya Kerjaya 2.0 applications
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 7 — Four individuals were charged in the Sessions Court here today over false statements in applications for incentives under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 career programme, dating back to two years ago. Foo Yon is accused of submitting a Daya Kerjaya 2.0 Employee Confirmation Form on behalf of his company to a Perkeso agent at Taman Bukit Serdang, Seri Kembangan, on November 2, 2024. Four individuals were charged in the Sessions Court here today over false statements in applications for incentives under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 career programme, dating back to two years ago.

items.title: Perikatan and BN in negotiations for Melaka, Hadi says goal remains to ‘unite and save the Malays’
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang today confirmed that preliminary discussions have begun between Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) on seat allocations for the upcoming Melaka state election. “The Melaka state assembly has not been dissolved, but discussions, particularly on Malay Muslim unity, are ongoing. He added that the negotiations would take into account the outcome of the last general election, when BN failed to secure any parliamentary seats in Melaka.

items.title: Anwar extends condolences to family of former CJ Mohamed Eusoff Chin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has extended his condolences to the entire family of former Chief Justice Tun Mohamed Eusoff Chin, who died this morning. In a Facebook post today, Anwar said Mohamed Eusoff had rendered great service to the nation, particularly in strengthening the judicial institution throughout his career. Mohamed Eusoff, 91, was laid to rest at the Section 9 Muslim Cemetery in Kota Damansara.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh, KL mayor sample Kuching’s culinary scene
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh and Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud sampled a taste of Kuching’s culinary scene on Friday morning as part of their visit to the city. The two, who arrived in Kuching for a series of engagements, began the day with a visit to Kuching South Mayor Dato Wee Hong Seng. Wee later accompanied them to the Borneo Culinary World Cup (BCWC) 2026 at Chung Hua Primary School No.

items.title: Sarawak implements Education Ministry’s Child Protection Policy, parents among those required to sign compliance pledge
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Sarawak began implementing the Ministry of Education’s (MoE) Child Protection Policy (CPP) on July 27, months after the nationwide rollout was announced in January. Sarawak Education director Omar Mahli said the State Education Department has directed all district education offices to immediately implement the policy after receiving MoE Circulars (SPI) No. Under the CPP, individuals dealing with students and schools are required to sign a Student Protection Policy Compliance Pledge (Aku Janji), a core component of the policy.

items.title: N. Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim helms finance, security and investment portfolios
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim will lead three major portfolios in the state government administration for the 2026-2031 term, including Islamic Religious Affairs and Security; Finance, Land and Natural Resources; and Investment, Infrastructure, Utilities, Communications and Felda. The Juasseh state assemblyman also announced the appointment of ten State Government Councilors including retaining two Exco members, namely Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli (Linggi) and Mustapha Nagoor (Palong). Mohd Faizal was appointed as the Rural Development and Regional Development Exco, while Mustapha will retain his old portfolio as the Youth and Sports Development Exco.

items.title: Three men arrested after leading police on car chase in Sibu
items.summary: SIBU, Aug 7 — Three local men were arrested after allegedly leading police on a chase before being detained in Sungai Merah on Friday, with officers also seizing suspected housebreaking tools found inside their vehicle. Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the incident occurred at about 1.30am when a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) team conducting crime prevention patrols spotted a suspicious Toyota Vios at the Paradom roundabout. Abang Zainal said three local men were detained for further investigation, while police also seized the car and several items believed to be commonly used for housebreaking, including a bolt cutter and a metal pry tool.

items.title: Unsafe George Town heritage properties to be shuttered, MBPP vows strict enforcement on owners
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 7 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) is considering engaging qualified engineers to conduct visual inspections of heritage buildings within the George Town World Heritage Site. MBPP Mayor Datuk A. Rajendran said the city council is also considering introducing a requirement for heritage building owners to submit a structural assessment report to the council every two years. He said MBPP has identified 66 heritage buildings within the George Town World Heritage Site as being poorly maintained.

items.title: Serian joins Kuching, Samarahan as unhealthy API readings rise
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 7 — Serian recorded the highest unhealthy reading on the Air Pollutant Index (API) in Sarawak as of noon today, with a reading of 162. Three districts in Sarawak are now recording unhealthy API readings, consisting of Serian, Samarahan and Kuching. Other districts in Sarawak records moderate readings, ranging from 57 to 91.

items.title: Hadi says Bersatu no longer part of Perikatan after plans for new coalition
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang has claimed that Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) is no longer a member of Perikatan Nasional (PN) after the party announced plans to form a new political coalition. Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Abdul Hadi said the PN constitution provides that any party choosing to join or establish another alliance would automatically cease to be a member of the coalition. “They (Bersatu) have already stated their intention to want to form another ‘team’.

items.title: ‘No more warnings’: Immigration D-G vows action against rogue officers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — The Immigration Department will not protect any of its officers and personnel involved in misconduct, including corruption or abuse of power, and immediate stern action will instead be taken against them without compromise. We will take immediate action (against officers involved in misconduct),” he said in his speech at the department’s monthly assembly here today. Citing the hacking of the Malaysian Immigration System (MyIMMs) involving the PLKS application and approval process, Zakaria said the department had received initial information on the involvement of its officers and personnel in the case.

items.title: Taxi drivers can replace vehicles with models other than Proton S70, says APAD
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 7 — Taxi drivers are allowed to license or replace their vehicles with models other than the Proton S70 under the National Madani Taxi Renewal Programme (Teksi Madani). This applies although the Transport Ministry’s policy announced on April 23 stipulated that new applications or taxi replacements under the programme would be voluntary and limited to the purchase of the Proton S70 taxi package offered under the programme. “Taxi drivers are encouraged to switch to Teksi Madani to enjoy the various incentives offered.

items.title: Technician pleads not guilty to seven counts of sexually assaulting 14-year-old stepdaughter
items.summary: IPOH, August 7 — A technician was charged in the Sessions Court here today with seven counts of sexually assaulting his 14-year-old stepdaughter for the past three years in Bandar Universiti, Seri Iskandar. He was also charged with committing similar offences against the same victim in May 2024 and May 2025 at the same location. Nor Arfahanim urged the court to deny bail, arguing that the accused posed a risk of interfering with the victims and prosecution witnesses.

items.title: Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in Jakarta was not flying aircraft, says Malaysia Aviation Group
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 7 — Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) has clarified that the Malaysia Airlines pilot detained in a recent incident was not operating the aircraft, saying flight safety was not compromised. MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said operational safety and crew fitness for duty remained non-negotiable at the group. MAG said it had commenced the first phase of mandatory drug screening for all pilots across its airlines, beginning with all 1,260 Malaysia Airlines pilots.

items.title: MACC-Customs anti-smuggling task force still under discussion, says department
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 7 — The proposed joint task force between the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to combat smuggling and revenue leakages has yet to be finalised, with discussions between both agencies still ongoing. In a response to Malay Mail the Customs Department said the proposed collaboration remained at the discussion stage and further details would be announced once both parties reached an agreement. C4 Centre head of research and policy advocacy Arief Hamzan said while the proposed task force was a positive step towards addressing enforcement weaknesses, its role, powers and implementation mechanisms must be clearly defined.

items.title: MCMC: Under-16 social media restrictions aim to ensure greater platform accountability
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Aug 7 — Malaysia’s regulatory approach to restricting social media access for users under 16 underscores the need for platforms to practice higher levels of accountability in ensuring a safe online environment, the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said. She said platform providers, as the developers and providers of social media products, should determine the safety features within the online environment. On June 1, Malaysia began enforcing its under-16 social media safeguards, requiring social media platforms to implement measures aimed at strengthening online safety and protecting young users.

items.title: Ten assemblymen sworn in as N. Sembilan exco members
items.summary: Linggi assemblyman Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli and Palong assemblyman Datuk Mustapha Nagoor were retained as Exco members. The new appointees are Chembong assemblyman Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Chennah assemblyman Siow Kong Choon, Labu assemblywoman Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Lenggeng assemblyman Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Sungai Lui assemblyman Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Gemencheh assemblyman Suhaimizan Bizar, Serting assemblyman Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Sikamat assemblyman Datuk Razali Abu Samah. Also present at the swearing-in ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz reminds new N. Sembilan exco to reject abuse of power, prioritise people
items.summary: KUALA PILAH, Aug 7 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has reminded the state’s new executive councillors (Exco) to carry out the trust placed on them and their responsibilities with honesty, fairness and professionalism. Accompanying His Royal Highness at the ceremony were Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-’Abidin Tuanku Muhriz. Tuanku Muhriz said the appointments represented a challenge for all the Exco members, who also serve as state assemblymen for their respective constituencies.

items.title: Terengganu technician loses RM58,500 in scam promising Indonesia export approval
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 7 — A women technician lost RM58,500 after falling victim to a scam offering to obtain a Food and Drug Administration (BPOM) certificate for the purpose of exporting products to Indonesia. Kuala Terengganu district police chief ACP Azli Mohd Noor said on March 23, 2024, the 38-year-old victim saw an advertisement related to Jom Eksport Ke Indonesia on Wan Muhd Ali’s Facebook social page. For Malaysian companies wishing to export food or health products to Indonesia, BPOM registration or approval is usually required depending on the type of product,” he said in a statement today.
